complete_examples.text: However the wheels and the rails are generally kept contact in the dynamic matrices, it is therefore difficult to characterize the wheel/rail separations and the geometrical contact/creepage in three-dimensional (3-D) space.

For example, Dinh et al. [26] presented a formulation of three-dimensional dynamic interactions between a bridge and a high-speed train, in which the classical theories such Hertz’s theory [27] and Kalker linear rolling contact theory [28] are applied to identify the wheel/rail vertical and lateral contact by finite tensionless and contact stiffness and creepage damping.
Besides the refinement and nonlinear wheel-rail contact geometry, creepage and force in a 3-D space are roughly considered as two-dimensional (2-D) contact and linear creep scenario.

The wheel–rail contact geometry and creepage in 3D space have been accurately depicted, and the dynamic equations of motion for vehicle–track system were solved by a fast explicit integration method by the author.

Regarding the differences in wheel–rail contact/creepage descriptions, i.e. rigid contact [7–9, 14–17], elastic contact [3, 18–20] and elastic-plastic contact [21–23], the complexity, accuracy and efficiency of the model are significantly different.

In another aspect, the complementarity-based methods have also been widely used in establishing vehicle–track interaction, but still having drawbacks on characterization of wheel–rail contact geometry/creepage in three-dimensional space.

Following these two key problems, a novel model that combines the essences of a refinement wheel– rail coupling model (Zhai, 2015) in characterizing the wheel–rail contact geometry/creepage and the energy principle in deriving the dynamic equations of motion will be proposed.

In the contact ellipse coordinate, the wheel-rail creep forces can be obtained by [23] Cf, i, j = −fc, i, jCi, j T (2) where fc, i, j denotes the creep coefficients and Ci, j denotes the creepage; the subscripts “i” and “j” denotes the i-th wheelset and the j-th side of the wheelset, j = l, r denote the left- and right-side.
